CEPA  (ALLIUM).

Common  Onion.  Liliaceoe.


In  use  as  a  medicine  since  time  immemorial.  Among  the  Egyptians  it
■was  hung  up  in  noxious  corners,  carried  about  with  one,  taken  for  the
consequences  of  bad  water,  used  for  the  sting  of  insects,  animal  poisons,
even  the  bite  of  the  mad  dog;  it  was  applied  as  an  irritant  and  to  mature
abscesses,  even  carbuncles;  then  it  was  used  for  frozen  feet,  by  Dioscoiides,
who  states  that  it  is  "  efficacious  when  feet  are  rubbed  sore,"  a  symptom  con-
firmed by  the  provings  and  verified  in  our  practice.  Then  it  was  also  used
as  a  remedy  for  promoting  the  growth  of  hair  and  hoofs,  as  also  for  de-
stroying warts  and  corns;  it  was  given  for  the  eequelse  of  "  white  and  black
measles  in  the  body."  Dioscorides  gave  it  for  podagra.  It  was  consid-
ered an  eye-remedy  and  an  ear-remedy,  serviceable  in  angina  and  for  loos-
ening mucus  if  it  rattled  in  the  throat  and  bronchia  of  children  and  old
people.  It  was  given  against  flatulence  and  to  promote  the  catamenia  as
well  as  the  flow  of  urine.  Dioscorides,  and  physicians  following  him,
among  the  Arabians,  had  a  glimpse  of  the  truth  of  similia,  for  they  used
the  onion  to  cure  the  symptoms  they  knew  it  was  capable  of  producing ;
but  with  Galen  all  reasonable  investigation  ceased.

It  is  mentioned  in  the  Old  Testament  under  the  name  Bejel,  which  the
Hebrews  craved,  as  in  our  time,  coflTee  and  tobacco  are  craved.

Homer  mentions  it  in  Iliad  XI,  629,  and  in  Odyssey  XIX,  233.

Herodotus,  Hist.  II,  Euterpe  N.  125.

Hippocrates,  Dediaete,  II,  359  ;  De  afi"ect.,  529;  De  Morbo  Sacro,  802.

ture prepared  from  the  red  Connecticut  onion ;  he  was  assisted  by  Drs.
Jeanes  (whose  preparations  were  made  in  water  up  to  fourth  dilution),

Alliborn  and  Raue._  See  American  Drug  Provings,  or  translation  therefrom
